Subject: Recap + asks: integration architecture and observability hooks

Marissa, appreciate the time today — quick recap and a list of asks so our engineering team can start sizing the POC work. I captured the main integration topics we discussed and prioritized them.

High-level summary (from our side)
- Goal: ML-powered answers in our analyst UI with 95th %-ile latency <200ms for short prompts; batch ranking for nightly jobs.
- Scope for POC: SDK setup, auth method (API key vs mTLS), routing to dev vs prod model variants, structured outputs for tool-calling (invoice parsing & enrichment), embeddings + reranker for result ranking, observability hooks (trace ids, latency breakdown, log fields).

Priority asks (please confirm feasibility / owners / rough estimates)
1) SDK quickstart and sample: we need a short Node + Python snippet showing auth, streaming, and structured output parsing.
2) Auth options: requirement is least-privilege keys + rotation; option for mutual TLS for production—what does Redwood support out of the box?
3) Routing & fallbacks: want deterministic routing for critical endpoints (single-tenant dev -> prod fallback) and an automatic fallback to lower-capacity model when capacity constrained.
4) Embeddings + reranker flow: expected size of vectors, recommended quantization, and latency tradeoffs for on-the-fly vs batched reranking.
5) Observability hooks: end-to-end trace id propagation, recommended header names, token-level latency breakdown header, and an example dashboard (latency by route, model, and compute).

Logistics
- We have a sandbox cluster (k8s) and a staging GCP project ready.
- Can you send a lightweight mutual action plan (timeline + deliverables) and any integration checklist?

Attachments: our internal tech brief (see link above).

Next steps: a) please share the checklist + sample code b) propose a technical deep-dive slot (30–45m) next week with your architects (we'd like Sergio/Karthik on your side).

Thanks — Aditi
Aditi Menon
VP, Platform Engineering | Bluefin Analytics

Subject: Re: Recap + asks: integration architecture and observability hooks — technical notes

Marissa / Aditi — following up with concrete recommendations I promised on the call. I tried to keep this concise and pragmatic for a POC.

A. SDK & Auth- Node/Python SDKs will support: API key header (Authorization: Bearer <key>), token rotation via our Console, and short-lived session tokens for ephemeral workloads. For Private (VPC) we can enable mTLS with client certs. For POC we recommend starting with API keys + IP-restricted keys, then switch to mTLS in staging.

B. Headers & Trace propagation (recommended)- Trace id: X-Redwood-Trace-Id (32 hex chars) — required for correlating request -> model spans.
- Parent span id (optional): X-Redwood-Parent-Id- Latency breakdown (summary header): X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: total=120ms;queue=10ms;compute=95ms;kv-cache=15ms- Sampling header for debug traces: X-Redwood-Trace-Sample: 1 (capture), 0 (ignore)- Request metadata: X-Redwood-Route: <route-name>

Notes: include the trace id as part of logs and instrument server-side spans (ingress, queue, compute, write-back). If you use OpenTelemetry we recommend mapping X-Redwood-Trace-Id to trace.id for end-to-end visibility.

C. Structured output & tool-calling- For the POC we recommend a constrained JSON schema for tool results with a top-level "tool_calls" array and robust validation on the client to avoid injection. Example (pseudo):

{
  "response": "...human text...",
  "tool_calls": [
    {"tool": "invoice_parser", "args": {"pdf_url": "https://..."}, "result": {...}}
  ]
}

- SDKs will include a helper to validate tool call outputs and to serialize exceptions.

D. Embeddings + reranker pattern- Recommended approach for fast, high-quality results:
  1) Generate embeddings in a batched job (64–256 items) using 1536-d vectors (or smaller 768 if space constrained).
  2) Store vectors in FAISS/ANN with HNSW index for low-latency nearest neighbors.
  3) Use a small rerank model online: candidate N=50 from ANN, then re-rank top 10 with a lightweight cross-encoder.

Latency notes: ANN lookup typically 5–30ms depending on vector size & hardware; rerank will add 30–120ms. For your 200ms SLO we recommend: keep embedding dim <=1536 and push reranker to dedicated infer nodes or async rerank for non-blocking UI.

E. Dashboard & traces- We'll provide a sample Grafana dashboard with: P50/P95 token latency, request queue length, model compute ms, KV cache hit-rate, embeddings lookup latency, rerank time.

I'll add the suggested headers and a small sample dashboard JSON to the shared Drive (link in MAP). Sergio — I'll leave final ops knobs to you (sampling rate defaults, log retention).

Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
